THE VERTICAL EXPLORER

Helicopter.

Taking off vertically and holding position in the air opens up missions that fixed-wing airplanes approach very differently.

01 / THE BIG PICTURE

Meet the helicopter.

A helicopter is a rotorcraft. Its engine-driven rotor blades generate lift without requiring forward motion in the same way as a fixed wing. Many helicopters can hover and move forward, backward, or sideways.

SPOT IT IN THE SKY

Look for the large rotor above the cabin and, on conventional designs, a smaller tail rotor. Skids are common on lighter helicopters.

02 / DESIGN DETAILS

What makes it different.

01

Main rotor

Rotating airfoil-shaped blades provide lift and help control the direction of flight.

02

Anti-torque system

Many helicopters use a tail rotor to counter the turning effect of the main rotor. Other layouts use different solutions.

03

Skids or wheels

Landing gear varies with the size and intended use of the helicopter.

04

Flight controls

Collective, cyclic, and anti-torque controls let the pilot manage rotor thrust and aircraft orientation.

03 / HOW IT WORKS

The engineering
behind the flight.

The main rotor accelerates air downward to create lift. Changing blade pitch adjusts rotor thrust, while cyclic control tilts the rotor’s lift direction to move the helicopter. In a conventional single-main-rotor design, the tail rotor helps control heading and counter torque.

04 / IN THE REAL WORLD

Made for a mission.

  • Search and rescue and medical transport
  • Access to offshore or remote locations
  • Inspection, observation, and specialized lifting
CAPABILITIES & TRADEOFFS

Helicopters offer hovering and vertical access, but rotor systems are mechanically complex. Compared with many fixed-wing aircraft, they typically sacrifice cruising efficiency and speed for this flexibility.

05 / A CLOSER LOOK

Good questions.

Can helicopters land anywhere?

No. A landing area must be suitable for the aircraft, with adequate clearance and acceptable surface, weather, and operating conditions. Access and aviation rules also apply.

Do all helicopters have tail rotors?

No. Tandem-rotor, coaxial, and other designs manage torque differently.

This guide describes an aircraft category. Equipment, speed, range, capacity, and operating limitations vary by model and configuration. Categories can overlap: a propeller aircraft can also be a cargo plane or seaplane.
